notes: §1985:VI.6.10.3 SR2: "If literal-1 is numeric, then it must be an unsigned integer." VersionConformancePass#VisitDisplayStatement asks Cobol85OperandForms#IsUnsignedIntegerLiteral (no sign written, a single INTEGERLIT token) of every numeric literal operand and checks construct display-numeric-literal-2002, so 85 refuses COBOL0900 and 2002 on accepts (the witness DISPLAY 1.5 prints 1.5 at 2002). Probes at 85: refused -1, +1, -0, +0, 1.0, .5, 1.5E2, "A" 1.5 (second operand) and 1,5 under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA; accepted and printed 0, 0001, 18-digit 123456789012345678, 999999999999999999 "X", ZERO and ALL "1" (figurative constants are not numeric literals). Classes a, e and the edited/group class do not reach a literal rule.

next.reason: 1985: "If literal-1 is numeric, then it must be an unsigned integer."; 2023: "DISPLAY syntax rules 14.9.11.3 restrict only identifier-1, mnemonic-name-1, identifier-2/3; no rule on numeric literal-1". The 2023 DISPLAY syntax rules cover the statement but no longer require a numeric literal-1 to be an unsigned integer. The GOBACK/STOP literal rules belong to other statements.
